clinical_category: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control

semantic_correction.stem: A nurse manager is reviewing an unexplained controlled-substance loss. Which set of findings is specifically listed by DEA as relevant when determining whether the loss is significant?

options.A: A pattern of losses over time, whether losses appear random, and efforts made to resolve them.
options.B: The employee's shift assignment, years of service, and whether the medication is brand-name or generic.
options.C: The unit's daily census, the time medications are delivered, and how often staff rotate assignments.
options.D: The medication's purchase price, the number of prescribers on the unit, and the age of the storage cabinet.

semantic_correction.rationale: DEA's Theft or Loss Q&A lists factors a registrant should consider when determining whether a controlled-substance loss is significant. One listed factor is a pattern of losses over a specific time period, whether the losses appear random, and the results of efforts taken to resolve the losses. DEA also lists the quantity and specific substance lost, association with access by specific individuals or unique activities, diversion potential, and local trends. Options B, C, and D contain operational details that are not listed as significance factors in this DEA guidance.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Recognize DEA-listed factors used to evaluate whether a controlled-substance loss is significant, including loss patterns, randomness, and efforts to resolve discrepancies.

audit_findings_append.finding: The original correct answer was uniquely longest. The revised item preserves the exact DEA factor set while presenting all choices as comparable operational triads, eliminating structural cueing and keeping one uniquely supported answer.

option_audit.A: Correct. DEA explicitly lists loss pattern over time, randomness, and results of resolution efforts together as a significance factor.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. Shift, tenure, and brand/generic status are not listed as the DEA significance factors tested here.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Census, delivery timing, and staff rotation are not the DEA-listed factor set.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. Purchase price, prescriber count, and cabinet age are not the DEA-listed factor set.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A reproduces a specific DEA-listed factor set; the other triads do not match the DEA guidance.
cueing_check: All four options are three-part operational factor sets of comparable length and syntax; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies A.
